title: I Took the Wedding Rehearsal Seating Chart to the Coordinator

parts.text: I stood at the altar two hours late because my mother had rearranged the place cards while the. I am twenty-seven, dental receptionist, I keep notes, I had a binder. The rehearsal was supposed to be simple. My mother, Elaine, had other plans involving my cousin Brooke in the front row because Brooke "photograph better." I found my fiance's grandmother, Rosa, assigned to a garden table behind a speaker. Rosa uses a cane and hates bass. I picked up the card. Elaine appeared in silk. "Don't touch. I paid for flowers." I said, "You paid for hydrangeas. You did not buy Rosa." The venue smelled like carpet cleaner and warm chafing fuel. My fiance, Malik, was parking his uncle. Elaine lowered her voice. "If Rosa sits front, people will look at the cane." I stared at her. "Say that again." She smiled for a passing groomsman. "You always make me the villain." The coordinator, Jess, came back smelling like mint gum. I held the card. "Who authorized a seating change?" Jess frowned. "Nobody. That's my chart." Elaine laughed. "I'm the mother." Jess looked at me, then at the binder where I had printed the original layout at 2:14 p.m. Elaine's version had a new filename in her email: FINAL_seating_ignore_Jess. I know because she had CC'd the florist and not me. Jess's phone buzzed with the florist asking which chart was real. Malik walked in. "What happened?" Water in the vase was already bleeding ink over the remaining cards, including ours.
parts.cliffhanger_hint: She tore the grandmother's card into the flowers and the ink is spreading onto the actual wedding seating.

social.video_title: She hid Grandma behind the speaker — Part 1/2
social.description: A two-hour-late rehearsal, a binder, and a seating file named ignore Jess. The hydrangeas got the torn place card. Would you have handed the coordinator the email?

parts.text: I pulled the torn pieces out of the vase, dripping on the carpet cleaner smell, and laid them. "Elaine, you don't get a secret chart," I said. Malik looked at the filename on my phone. He is quiet until he is not. "Mom is not even your mother," he told Elaine, which was technically true, she is mine, and still the right temperature. Jess reprinted from the 2:14 file and moved Rosa front, aisle, cane visible, beloved. Elaine sat in the back during rehearsal and texted the family group that I had humiliated her over flowers. I muted it. At dinner I gave a toast that mentioned hydrangeas only as flowers, not as weapons. Rosa squeezed my hand. The next morning Elaine called the venue to "restore dignity." Jess forwarded me the voicemail. I let Malik listen. He called his own mother, who is actually kind, and asked her to run day-of logistics. Elaine still came to the wedding. She did not touch cards. I had Jess put a staffer on the table. Brooke took beautiful photos from the second row and did not implode. After the cake, Elaine said, "I only wanted it to look nice." I said, "Nice isn't moving a woman with a cane behind a subwoofer." She cried in the bathroom. I ate cake. Weeks later she mailed a card with a pressed hydrangea and no apology. I tell patients I am good at charts. I am.

social.video_title: The 2:14 chart beat the hydrangeas — Part 2/2
social.description: Jess reprinted the original file and Grandma sat on the aisle. Day-of logistics went to the kind mother. Would you have filed the pressed flower with no apology?
